stages.title: Using HDI to compare development
stages.sub: What HDI adds compared to GDP, and where it still falls short.

steps.q: Two countries have the same income per person, but one has much longer life expectancy and more years in school. Would GDP alone show this difference?
steps.right: No, GDP only looks at income
steps.hint: GDP is a measure of output and income only.

steps.right: Yes, straight away from the numbers
steps.wrong: No, you would need separate reports for each
steps.hint: Think about what a single combined score, calculated the same way everywhere, lets you do.

steps.q: HDI adds breadth beyond income, ranks countries on one scale, and uses data that is easy to collect, yet it still averages away gaps between rich and poor within a country. Overall, does HDI give a perfect picture of development?
steps.right: No, it still has drawbacks despite its strengths
steps.wrong: Yes, once income, health and education are combined it is complete
steps.hint: Think about what the hidden inequality problem, and other gaps like this, mean for how much you can trust the single score.
